rawFindings.title: Content hash for cache busting removed in karma middleware
rawFindings.explanation: The code changed to append the file's modification time (mtime) instead of the SHA hash for cache busting on script and style file URLs. Previously, the unique SHA-1 hash of the file content was used, which accurately reflects content changes. Using mtime.getTime() is less reliable because file system timestamps may not change with every content modification or may have insufficient resolution.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to using file.sha (SHA-1 of content) for cache busting query parameters as it was before the change.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: When a file's content changes but its modification time does not update (e.g., due to file system caching or low resolution timestamps), the browser cache will not be invalidated properly, causing outdated files to be served, leading to stale tests or unexpected behavior.

rawFindings.title: File mtime used instead of SHA in mapping object string formatting
rawFindings.explanation: In the generated script mappings, the code uses file.mtime.getTime() instead of the SHA string representing the content hash. Previously, the mapping associated URLs with SHA strings, providing an accurate content version identifier. Using mtime as integer may be less precise and different in type than before, which might affect consumers expecting string hashes.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert the return string to use file.sha as the version identifier as before.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Consumers of the mapping expecting a SHA string get a millisecond timestamp instead, which may cause mismatches or cache issues if the mtime is not sufficiently precise or updated.

rawFindings.title: Removed SHA computation in preprocessor potentially breaks file content hashing
rawFindings.explanation: The change removes the SHA hash computation of the file content by deleting the preprocessor function that set file.sha. Consequently, file.sha property will be undefined or not set, which causes the middleware (karma.js) to no longer have reliable content hashes for cache busting and mappings, as it relies on file.sha.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the preprocessor function that computes the SHA hash and adds file.sha property to the file object during preprocessing.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: file.sha is undefined after preprocessing. The karma middleware attempts to append file.sha to URLs and mappings but now gets undefined or absent values. This breaks cache invalidation and correctness of served files.
